tweet_summary: A viral list claims real-terms GDP-per-capita growth for each UK Prime Minister, with suspiciously low/uneven figures (e.g. tiny growth for big-reform PMs) implying decline under recent leaders and during mass immigration.
why_note_decision: The per-PM figures do not match the standard ONS chained-volume-measure of real GDP per capita; multiple commenters (and ONS/World Bank data) show much higher cumulative growth for pre-2010 PMs (e.g. Thatcher's ~11yr term at ~2%/yr compounds to roughly +25-29%, not single-digit). The post presents a non-standard/incorrect calculation as authoritative economic fact, so a sourced correction is warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note (1) states the post's per-PM figures do not use the standard ONS chained-volume-measure of real GDP per capita and are materially wrong/understated for most pre-2010 PMs, (2) gives at least one concrete corrected figure with the right order of magnitude (e.g. Thatcher cumulative real GDP-per-capita growth ~+25% to +29%, NOT ~+2-3%), and (3) cites an authoritative source (ONS time series IHXW or World Bank NY.GDP.PCAP.KD for GB). Do NOT pass a note that merely calls the post 'opinion', that endorses the post's numbers, or that argues immigration/political points without correcting the methodology.
reference_note: The figures do not use the standard chained volume measure of real GDP per capita; official ONS and World Bank data show much higher growth for most pre-2010 PMs, e.g. +29% under Thatcher (not +2.7%). https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/grossdomesticproductgdp/timeseries/ihxw/pn2 https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.PCAP.KD?locations=GB

fact_check.claim_verdict: misleading - figures use a non-standard/incorrect measure that understates real GDP-per-capita growth for most pre-2010 PMs
fact_check.notes: UK trend real growth post-1980 ~2%/yr; over Thatcher's 11+ years that compounds to roughly +25-29% cumulative, consistent with the note. Standard metric is ONS chained volume measure (CVM). The post's figures are internally inconsistent with that measure.

importance.lens_rationale: 1.2M impressions on an economic-decline narrative tied to immigration politics; correcting fabricated macro statistics supports informed public reasoning (progress lens).
